discrepancy_checks.detects: One reading far off the line of best fit
discrepancy_checks.diagnosis: A balance point misjudged - the rule was still creeping, or a distance was read from the wrong mark. Repeat that setting.

discrepancy_checks.detects: Measured table disagrees with the worked table beyond the band
discrepancy_checks.diagnosis: The rule was not balanced at its own centre mark first, so every distance carries the rule's own moment.

discrepancy_checks.detects: Recovered constant outside the tolerance band around the expected value
discrepancy_checks.diagnosis: Distances were measured from the rule's end instead of from the pivot - check the reference point of every distance.

bom_tiers.description: Plywood/MDF beam and pivot offcuts, hand-slid masses, phone/webcam reading of the marker against a printed scale, Arduino-class controller or direct PC control.
2020/2040 aluminium extrusion gantry beam, motorised carriages positioning both masses, tilt sensor reading the balance, dedicated microcontroller, enclosed E-stop panel.
Anodised extrusion + machined knife-edge pivot, encoded carriages, redundant tilt sensing, safety relay for the monitored stop, calibration certificate workflow in-app.

machine_design_hint.description: The gantry beam becomes the balance beam: it rests on a knife-edge pivot at its centre mark, one carriage positions the known mass along the beam, and a second carriage slides the unknown mass until the beam's tilt sensor reads level. The lesson states honestly that the machine finds the balance from a tilt sensor, while the candidate judges the horizontal by eye against a fixed mark.

graph_spec.form: linear, line of best fit through the origin region
graph_spec.notes: Axes labelled with quantity/unit; scale fills at least half the grid; slope from a large triangle. At balance M x a = X x b, so the slope of b against a is M/X and the unknown mass is X = M / slope.

observation_spec.precision_notes: Ruled table; column heads as quantity/unit; distances read to 0.1 cm from the pivot mark.

apparatus.name: pivot wedge
apparatus.specification: knife-edge or triangular prism for the rule to rest on

apparatus.name: unknown mass
apparatus.specification: the object whose mass is to be found, with a loop for hanging

apparatus.name: thread loops
apparatus.specification: for hanging the masses from the rule

apparatus.name: marker disc
apparatus.specification: painted high-contrast, fixed to the unknown mass for filming

hazards: falling masses if a thread loop slips off the rule
rule sliding off the pivot and dropping
hazard_profile.notes: Mechanics practical: no heat, electricity or chemicals. Keep feet clear of the fall line of the masses.

practical.outcome_spec: Recovered unknown mass within +/-5% of its true mass (target +/-3%), computed identically from the teacher's readings and from the filmed demonstration's tracked marker positions.
practical.subject: Physics
syllabus_refs: WAEC Physics syllabus: equilibrium of forces and moments (principle of moments) - as listed in third-party-hosted copies of the WAEC Physics syllabus; NOT yet confirmed against the official waecnigeria.org PDF or a serving WAEC teacher (see docs/TEACHER_VALIDATION.md).
practical.title: Principle of moments: mass of an object from a balanced metre rule

precautions: The metre rule was first balanced on the pivot at its own centre mark with no masses hung, so its own weight acted through the pivot and had no turning effect.
Each balance reading was taken only when the rule rested horizontal and steady, and distances were measured from the pivot mark to the thread loop, not to the edge of the mass.

steps.check_question: Why balance the empty rule first instead of going straight to the masses?
steps.expected_observation: Empty rule rests horizontal on the pivot at its centre mark.
steps.narration: Rest the metre rule on the pivot and slide it until it balances horizontally with nothing hung from it. Note the centre mark at the pivot.
safety_notes: Confirm the pivot is stable before resting the rule on it.
steps.title: Balance the empty rule at its centre

steps.check_question: From which mark is the distance a measured?
steps.expected_observation: Known mass hanging vertically at the chosen distance.
steps.narration: Hang the 100 g known mass from the rule on one side of the pivot, at a distance a of 12.0 cm from the pivot.
safety_notes: Support the mass from below while hanging it so it cannot drop suddenly.
steps.title: Hang the known mass at distance a

steps.check_question: Why slide the unknown mass instead of adding more known masses?
steps.expected_observation: Rule horizontal and steady with both masses hung.
steps.narration: Hang the unknown mass on the other side and slide it along the rule until the rule balances horizontally again. Read its distance b from the pivot.
steps.title: Slide the unknown mass to balance

steps.check_question: What pattern do you expect in b as a increases?
steps.expected_observation: A complete set of balance readings, one row per distance.
steps.narration: Repeat for a = 16, 20, 24 and 28 cm, sliding the unknown mass to a fresh balance each time and recording b.
steps.title: Repeat for a = 16, 20, 24, 28 cm

steps.check_question: Why does the graph pass through the origin region if the moments balance?
steps.expected_observation: A ruled table with quantity/unit column heads and consistent decimal places.
steps.narration: Tabulate the known mass, a and b for each balance.
steps.title: Tabulate a and b

steps.check_question: Why must the slope triangle be large?
steps.expected_observation: A straight line through the origin region; slope about 1.25.
steps.narration: Plot b against a. Draw the line of best fit and find the slope from a large triangle.
steps.title: Plot b against a and find the slope

steps.check_question: Why is the unknown mass M divided by the slope and not multiplied by it?
steps.expected_observation: Unknown mass approx. 80 g, within the tolerance band.
steps.narration: At balance, M times a equals X times b, so the slope of b against a is M over X. Evaluate the unknown mass X as M divided by the slope.
steps.title: Evaluate the unknown mass

steps.check_question: What would a changed balance point of the empty rule tell you?
steps.expected_observation: Empty rule still balances at its centre mark.
steps.narration: Take both masses off and check the empty rule still balances at its centre mark. If it has shifted, the earlier readings carry that shift.
steps.title: Recheck the empty balance

steps.check_question: Why is 'I avoided errors' not a creditworthy precaution?
steps.narration: State two precautions you took, in the past tense, naming the error you avoided and the action you took.
steps.title: State two precautions
